where: Section 3, last paragraph: 'A missing transition is a dead state ... Without that state, swapping finals can accept strings that should be rejected.'
problem: The direction of the error is backwards for a DFA. In an incomplete DFA a missing transition kills the run, so the string is rejected both before and after swapping finals. Completing is needed because the swapped machine wrongly rejects strings that belong to the complement, not because it wrongly accepts strings outside it. Over-acceptance after swapping finals is the NFA failure, not the incomplete-DFA failure. A student will learn the wrong reason for the construction.
fix: A missing transition kills the run: the string is rejected. If you swap final and nonfinal states without adding the dead state, those runs still die after swapping, so strings that belong to the complement are wrongly rejected. Add one nonfinal dead state for all missing transitions, make it loop on every symbol, then swap. (Swapping finals of an NFA is the case that wrongly accepts strings, because different runs of the same string end in different states.)

where: Worked example 1, steps 6 and 7 and the answer line
problem: Step 5 already shows (E,N) --1→ (E,F), so the string 1 (length 1) is already a witness. Step 6 instead reaches (E,F) through a length-3 detour, and the answer states 'witness length is 3'. That is true but misleads a reader into thinking 3 is the shortest witness.
fix: Add: the shortest witness is 1, since (E,N) --1→ (E,F) directly; 001 also works, and step 6 shows a longer path only to demonstrate reachability.

problem: 'For an NFA, track the set of possible states or convert to DFA; time is O(|w| × number of states)' mixes two very different costs. Tracking state sets costs O(|w| × |Q| × |Σ|) (or O(|w| × number of transitions)), while converting to a DFA can blow up to 2^|Q| states.
fix: For an NFA, simulate by carrying the set of possible states: O(|w| × |Q| × |Σ|). Converting to a DFA first is also correct but can cost up to 2^|Q| states, so simulate unless you need the DFA anyway.

problem: 'Take a complete DFA for L, add a dead state for every missing transition, then swap' contradicts itself: a complete DFA has no missing transitions, so the instruction to add dead states has nothing to attach to.
fix: Take a DFA for L, add one nonfinal dead state for the missing transitions (with self-loops on every symbol) so the machine becomes complete, then swap final and nonfinal states. The dead state becomes final, which is correct because every string that falls off the original machine is in the complement.

problem: Completeness is demanded only for B in the difference case. Union and intersection through the product also need both machines complete, otherwise δ_P((p,q),a) is undefined for a string that one machine accepts, and the product wrongly rejects it.
fix: Complete both A and B with nonfinal dead states before building the product, for every operation (union, intersection, difference). Then δ_P is total and the final-state rule for the chosen operation is sound.
